chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ḥātim, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from his father, who said:

A man wrote to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام asking him about the salat of the nawafil of the month of Ramadan and about increasing them. So he عليه السلام wrote back to him a letter, which I read in his own handwriting:

Pray in the first part of the month of Ramadan, over twenty nights, twenty rakʿahs. Pray eight rakʿahs of them between al-Maghrib and al-ʿAtamah, and after al-ʿIshaʾ twelve rakʿahs. And in the last ten nights, pray eight rakʿahs between al-Maghrib and al-ʿAtamah, and twenty-two rakʿahs after al-ʿAtamah, except on the night of the twenty-first and the twenty-third; then one hundred will suffice you, if Allah wills. And that is besides the fifty.
And increase your recitation of: “Indeed, We sent it down.”

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ: the opening words of Surah al-Qadr, recommended for frequent recitation
key_terms.الزِّيَادَةِ: an addition or increase in the number of prayers
key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: the night prayer time, referring here to al-ʿIshaʾ
key_terms.الْعَشْرِ الْأَوَاخِرِ: the last ten nights of Ramadan
key_terms.الْمِائَةَ: one hundred rakʿahs on the specified nights
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the sacred month of fasting

ai.seo_question: How many nawafil rakʿahs should be prayed in the nights of Ramadan according to Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the recommended nightly prayers of the month of Ramadan, specifying the number of rakʿahs for the first twenty nights and the last ten nights. It also gives special emphasis to the nights of the twenty-first and twenty-third and recommends frequent recitation of Surah al-Qadr.
